title: Extend chatbot/api/streaming.py with token streaming and typing indicators
description:
Extend chatbot/api/streaming.py to implement real token streaming with typing indicators and partial generation on the /chat/stream SSE path. The streaming endpoint must emit tokens as they arrive from the provider rather than waiting for the full response, and must emit typing indicator events.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- chatbot/api/streaming.py for the current SSE endpoint structure, router, and StreamRequest model
- chatbot/core/turn.py for how the pipeline calls the provider and produces a response
- chatbot/providers/ for any existing provider adapter streaming methods

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed paths. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed files modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

SINGLE-OWNER FILE: chatbot/api/streaming.py is owned exclusively by this task in this phase. No other task may modify it.

Implementation details:

1. Inspect the existing chatbot/api/streaming.py to understand the current SSE endpoint shape: the router variable name, prefix, the StreamRequest model, and how the existing handler returns a StreamingResponse.

2. Extend the POST /chat/stream handler to implement token streaming:
   - The handler must accept a `stream_tokens: bool = True` field in the request body (or query param) that controls whether tokens are streamed one-by-one or emitted in chunks.
   - The async generator must yield SSE events in the following order:
     a. `data: {"type": "typing", "status": "started"}\n\n` — typing indicator begins
     b. For each step in the pipeline that runs before the provider call (receive, retrieve, compile_context), emit SSE events as before: `data: {"step": "<name>", "status": "running"}\n\n` and completed events.
     c. When the provider call step begins, emit `data: {"step": "call_provider", "status": "streaming"}\n\n`.
     d. As tokens arrive from the provider (via a streaming adapter), emit each token as: `data: {"type": "token", "text": "<token_text>"}\n\n`.
       - If the provider does not support streaming or stream_tokens is False, emit the full response as before.
     e. After provider completes, emit `data: {"step": "call_provider", "status": "done", "duration_ms": <N>}\n\n`.
     f. Emit `data: {"type": "typing", "status": "stopped"}\n\n` — typing indicator ends.
     g. Run remaining pipeline steps (extract, respond) emitting their step events.
     h. Emit final response event and [DONE] terminator as before.
   - The typing indicator events (`started` and `stopped`) are emitted even when stream_tokens is False — they signal the UI to show/hide the typing bubble.

3. Ensure backward compatibility: the existing /chat/stream contract (returning step events and a final response) must still work. The token streaming is additive — clients that ignore token events will see the same final response event as before.

4. If the provider adapter does not expose streaming yet, token streaming is a no-op: the generator yields the full response as a single text block after the provider step completes. This ensures the endpoint is importable and functional before provider streaming is wired.

5. Ensure python -m py_compile chatbot/api/streaming.py passes.
acceptance_criteria: chatbot/api/streaming.py emits SSE typing indicator events ('started' and 'stopped')
chatbot/api/streaming.py supports token streaming via 'type': 'token' SSE events when stream_tokens is True
Token streaming falls back to full-response emission when provider does not support streaming
Existing step events (step: running, step: done) are preserved
Existing final response event and [DONE] terminator are preserved
The /chat/stream endpoint remains backward-compatible with existing clients
